การดำเนินงานของราชบัณฑิตยสถาน แบ่งเป็น ๒: The Royal Institute's operations were divided into 2 parts: the Council of Fellows and the civil service. The Council of Fellows set policy for academic work and consisted of council members who were Fellows from 3 academies, namely the Academy of Moral and Political Sciences, the Academy of Science and the Academy of Arts. The President of the Royal Institute was President of the Council, the Vice President of the Royal Institute was Vice President of the Council, the Secretary-General of the Royal Institute served as Secretary of the Council, and the Deputy Secretary-General served as Assistant Secretary of the Council. In the civil service part, the Secretary-General of the Royal Institute was head of the agency, assisted by the Deputy Secretary-General, overseeing the academic and administrative work of the Office of the Secretary, the Moral and Political Sciences Division, the Science Division and the Arts Division, and coordinating work with all the academies.
การดำเนินงานด้านวิชาการ ดำเนินงานในรูปขอ: Academic work is carried out through academic committees, which hold meetings to consider terms, coin technical terms, write explanations of terms in various fields and set language guidelines. The results, as bodies of knowledge, are then disseminated to the public through various channels, including print, radio, television and electronic media, so as to meet the public's needs widely. Feedback is also gathered in order to make services more effective.
การดำเนินงานแบ่งเป็น ๒ ส่วน คือ ราชบัณฑิ: The work is divided into two parts: the Royal Society, which sets academic policy, and the Office of the Royal Society, the permanent government agency.

การอ่านหมายเลขโทรศัพท์ ให้อ่านแบบเรียงตั: Telephone numbers are read digit by digit. Originally, the number 2 was read as โท (tho) so that the sounds of “2” and “3” would be distinct, since telephone numbers consist of many digits and sometimes several 2s and 3s appear in sequence, and the sounds of "2" and "3" are similar. Later, as telephone systems improved greatly and “2” was no longer confused with "3", the digit "2" in telephone numbers came to be read as สอง (song), for example: 0 2225 8622 is read สูน สอง-สอง-สอง-ห้า แปด-หก-สอง-สอง (sun song-song-song-ha paet-hok-song-song)

ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑ สัญลักษณ์ H เป็นแก๊สไม่ม: Element number 1, symbol H. A colourless, odourless, tasteless and highly flammable gas, the lightest of all gases. It has many uses, e.g. in the synthesis of ammonia and methyl alcohol and in the hydrogenation of vegetable oils.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐ สัญลักษณ์ Ne เป็นแก๊สเฉ: Element number 10, symbol Ne. An inert gas present at only 1 part in 55,000 in the atmosphere.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๐ สัญลักษณ์ Fm เป็นธาตุก: Element number 100, symbol Fm. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๑ สัญลักษณ์ Md เป็นธาตุก: Element number 101, symbol Md. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๒ สัญลักษณ์ No เป็นธาตุก: Element number 102, symbol No. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๓ สัญลักษณ์ Lr (ใช้ Lw ก: Element number 103, symbol Lr (Lw is also used). A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๔ สัญลักษณ์ Rf เป็นธาตุก: Element number 104, symbol Rf. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature. In the Soviet Union it was called kurchatovium, with the symbol Ku.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๕ สัญลักษณ์ Db (ยังไม่ได: Element number 105, symbol Db (not yet revised in the Royal Institute Dictionary)
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๖ สัญลักษณ์ Sg (ยังไม่ได: Element number 106, symbol Sg (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๗ สัญลักษณ์ Bh (ยังไม่ได: Element number 107, symbol Bh (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๘ สัญลักษณ์ Hs (ยังไม่ได: Element number 108, symbol Hs (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๐๙ สัญลักษณ์ Mt (ยังไม่ได: Element number 109, symbol Mt (not yet added to the Royal Institute Dictionary)
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๑ สัญลักษณ์ Na เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 11, symbol Na. A soft silvery-white metal that melts at 97.8 °C. Its most common important compound is table salt.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๒ สัญลักษณ์ Mg เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 12, symbol Mg. A metal; a silvery solid that melts at 650 °C. When ignited in air it burns with a brilliant white flame. Used in photography, incendiary bombs, lightweight alloys with other metals, etc.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๓ สัญลักษณ์ Al เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 13, symbol Al. A metal; a silvery-white solid that melts at 660 °C. It has many uses, e.g. alloyed with other metals and used to make kitchenware.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๔ สัญลักษณ์ Si เป็นอโลหะ: Element number 14, symbol Si. A non-metal; a solid that melts at 1410 °C. It makes up about 25 percent of the Earth's crust.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๕ สัญลักษณ์ P เป็นอโลหะ ล: Element number 15, symbol P. A non-metal; a solid with several allotropes. The main ones are white phosphorus (sometimes called yellow phosphorus), soft and waxy, melting at 44 °C, easily ignited, glowing on contact with air and highly toxic; and red phosphorus, a reddish-violet powder that does not glow in air, is hard to ignite and is not toxic like white phosphorus.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๖ สัญลักษณ์ S เป็นอโลหะ ล: Element number 16, symbol S. A non-metal; a solid with several allotropes. It has many uses, e.g. in the manufacture of sulfuric acid, in the rubber industry, and in making match heads, gunpowder, fireworks and medicines; sulfa drugs and penicillin also contain sulfur.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๗ สัญลักษณ์ Cl เป็นอโลหะ: Element number 17, symbol Cl. A non-metal; a greenish-yellow toxic gas with a pungent, choking odour. Used to disinfect water, in the manufacture of hydrochloric acid and bleaching powder; many insecticides, such as DDT, contain chlorine as a key component.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๘ สัญลักษณ์ Ar เป็นแก๊สเฉ: Element number 18, symbol Ar. An inert gas making up about 0.94 percent of air by volume. Used to fill light bulbs and fluorescent tubes.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๑๙ สัญลักษณ์ K เป็นโลหะ ลั: Element number 19, symbol K. A metal; a soft silvery-white solid that melts at 63.7 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒ สัญลักษณ์ He เป็นแก๊สเฉื: Element number 2, symbol He. An inert gas present at only 1 part in 200,000 in the atmosphere.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๐ สัญลักษณ์ Ca เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 20, symbol Ca. A metal; a soft white solid that melts at 838 °C. An important component of bones, teeth, marble and limestone.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๑ สัญลักษณ์ Sc เป็นโลหะที: Element number 21, symbol Sc. A rare metal; a white solid that melts at 1539 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๒ สัญลักษณ์ Ti เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 22, symbol Ti. A metal; a solid that melts at 1668 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๓ สัญลักษณ์ V เป็นโลหะ ลั: Element number 23, symbol V. A metal; a white solid that melts at 1900 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๔ สัญลักษณ์ Cr เป็นโลหะแข: Element number 24, symbol Cr. A hard silvery metal that melts at 1875 °C. Used in the manufacture of stainless steel, extra-strong steel for tools, and in chrome plating.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๕ สัญลักษณ์ Mn เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 25, symbol Mn. A metal; a hard but brittle silvery solid that melts at 1245 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๖ สัญลักษณ์ Fe เป็นโลหะลั: Element number 26, symbol Fe. A metal; a lustrous silvery-white solid that melts at 1536 °C. It has many uses, e.g. making cast iron, wrought iron and steel.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๗ สัญลักษณ์ Co เป็นโลหะแข: Element number 27, symbol Co. A hard silvery metal that melts at 1495 °C. Alloyed with other metals to give them special properties; for example, with iron it makes it harder, and magnets made from it are exceptionally strong. Cobalt compounds are used to give a blue colour in the glass and ceramics industries.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๘ สัญลักษณ์ Ni เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 28, symbol Ni. A metal; a silvery solid that melts at 1453 °C. Used in alloys with other metals, for plating other metals, etc.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๒๙ สัญลักษณ์ Cu เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 29, symbol Cu. A metal; a soft red solid that melts at 1083 °C. It is easily beaten into thin sheets and drawn into wire, and is a good conductor of heat and electricity.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓ สัญลักษณ์ Li เป็นโลหะ ลั: Element number 3, symbol Li. A metal; a silvery solid, the lightest of all solid metals. Melts at 180.5 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๐ สัญลักษณ์ Zn เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 30, symbol Zn. A metal; a bluish-white solid that melts at 419 °C. It has many uses, e.g. in alloys with other metals and for coating iron against rust.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๑ สัญลักษณ์ Ga เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 31, symbol Ga. A silvery-white metal; a solid that melts at 29.78 °C and boils at 2100 °C. Used in high-temperature thermometers; the compound gallium arsenide is used as a semiconductor.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๒ สัญลักษณ์ Ge เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 32, symbol Ge. A brittle white metal that melts at 937.4 °C. It has semiconducting properties; the compound magnesium germanate is used in fluorescent lamps.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๓ สัญลักษณ์ As ลักษณะเป็น: Element number 33, symbol As. A solid with 3 allotropes: grey, black and yellow arsenic. A highly toxic element.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๔ สัญลักษณ์ Se เป็นอโลหะ: Element number 34, symbol Se. A non-metal with chemical properties similar to sulfur; a solid that melts at 217 °C. Used to make photoelectric cells.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๕ สัญลักษณ์ Br เป็นอโลหะ: Element number 35, symbol Br. A non-metal; a dark red liquid that evaporates easily, with a strong pungent odour; toxic and irritating to the nasal membranes. Boils at 58.8 °C. Bromine compounds are used in medicine and photography.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๖ สัญลักษณ์ Kr เป็นแก๊สเฉ: Element number 36, symbol Kr. An inert gas present at only 1 part in 670,000 in the atmosphere.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๗ สัญลักษณ์ Rb เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 37, symbol Rb. A metal; a soft white solid that is extremely reactive chemically. Melts at 38.9 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๘ สัญลักษณ์ Sr เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 38, symbol Sr. A metal; a soft pale yellow solid that is chemically reactive. Melts at 752 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๓๙ สัญลักษณ์ Y เป็นโลหะ ลั: Element number 39, symbol Y. A metal; a dark grey solid that melts at 1500 °C. Used in alloys with other metals and in nuclear technology.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔ สัญลักษณ์ Be เป็นโลหะ ลั: Element number 4, symbol Be. A metal; a white solid that melts at 1277 °C. Used in corrosion-resistant alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๐ สัญลักษณ์ Zr เป็นโลหะหา: Element number 40, symbol Zr. A rare metal; a solid that melts at 1852 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๑ สัญลักษณ์ Nb เป็นโลหะหา: Element number 41, symbol Nb. A rare metal; a grey solid that melts at 2468 °C. Alloyed with stainless steel to make it resistant to corrosion and high temperatures.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๒ สัญลักษณ์ Mo เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 42, symbol Mo. A metal; a white solid that melts at 2610 °C. Used in alloys with other metals and in making steel.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๓ สัญลักษณ์ Tc เป็นธาตุกั: Element number 43, symbol Tc. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๔ สัญลักษณ์ Ru เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 44, symbol Ru. A metal; a brittle silvery solid that melts at 2310 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๕ สัญลักษณ์ Rh เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 45, symbol Rh. A metal; a silvery solid that melts at 1966 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๖ สัญลักษณ์ Pd เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 46, symbol Pd. A metal; a silvery solid similar to platinum that melts at 1552 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๗ สัญลักษณ์ Ag เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 47, symbol Ag. A fairly soft white metal that melts at 960.8 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๘ สัญลักษณ์ Cd เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 48, symbol Cd. A metal; a soft silvery solid that melts at 321 °C. A good absorber of neutrons, it is made into rods called control rods in nuclear reactors.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๔๙ สัญลักษณ์ In เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 49, symbol In. A metal; a soft silvery-white solid that melts at 156.2 °C. It has many uses, e.g. in electronic components, in dental alloys, and for plating silver-coated iron.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕ สัญลักษณ์ B เป็นโลหะ ลัก: Element number 5, symbol B. A metal in the form of a fine brown powder or yellow crystals that melts at 2300 °C. Used in the steel and glass industries.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๐ สัญลักษณ์ Sn เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 50, symbol Sn. A metal; a soft silvery-white solid that melts at 231.9 °C. It has 3 allotropes: grey tin, white tin and rhombic tin. Used to coat iron against rust and in alloys; thin tin foil is used to wrap things against moisture.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๑ สัญลักษณ์ Sb เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 51, symbol Sb. A metal; a brittle silvery-white solid that melts at 630.5 °C. It has the special property of expanding when it solidifies, and is used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๒ สัญลักษณ์ Te ลักษณะเป็น: Element number 52, symbol Te. A silvery-white solid with chemical properties similar to sulfur; melts at 449.5 °C. It has several allotropes and is used in alloys with other metals and in the coloured glass industry.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๓ สัญลักษณ์ I เป็นอโลหะ ล: Element number 53, symbol I. A non-metal; a lustrous grey-black solid that melts at 114 °C and sublimes into a violet vapour. An essential element for the thyroid gland; a deficiency causes goitre.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๔ สัญลักษณ์ Xe เป็นแก๊สเฉ: Element number 54, symbol Xe. An inert gas present at only 0.006 parts per million in the atmosphere.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๕ สัญลักษณ์ Cs เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 55, symbol Cs. A silvery metal that is highly reactive chemically. Melts at 28.7 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๖ สัญลักษณ์ Ba เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 56, symbol Ba. A metal; a soft silvery solid that tarnishes quickly in air. Melts at 714 °C. Barium compounds are used in the paint, glass and fireworks industries.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๗ สัญลักษณ์ La เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 57, symbol La. A metal; a white solid that melts at 920 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๘ สัญลักษณ์ Ce เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 58, symbol Ce. A soft grey metal that melts at 804 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๕๙ สัญลักษณ์ Pr เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 59, symbol Pr. A metal; a pale yellowish solid that melts at 935 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖ สัญลักษณ์ C เป็นอโลหะ ลั: Element number 6, symbol C. A non-metal; a solid with several allotropes, such as diamond and graphite. Carbon is one of the most important elements in living things.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๐ สัญลักษณ์ Nd เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 60, symbol Nd. A metal; a pale yellowish solid that melts at 1024 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๑ สัญลักษณ์ Pm เป็นธาตุกั: Element number 61, symbol Pm. A synthetic radioactive element that does not occur in nature; a solid that melts at 1027 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๒ สัญลักษณ์ Sm เป็นโลหะหา: Element number 62, symbol Sm. A rare metal; a solid that melts at 1072 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๓ สัญลักษณ์ Eu เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 63, symbol Eu. A metal; a very soft grey solid that melts at 826 °C. Used to absorb neutrons to control nuclear reactions, and as a phosphor in colour television sets, etc.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๔ สัญลักษณ์ Gd เป็นโลหะที: Element number 64, symbol Gd. A very rare metal; a solid that melts at 1312 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๕ สัญลักษณ์ Tb เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 65, symbol Tb. A metal; a solid that melts at 1356 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๖ สัญลักษณ์ Dy เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 66, symbol Dy. A metal; a solid that melts at 1407 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๗ สัญลักษณ์ Ho เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 67, symbol Ho. A metal; a lustrous solid that melts at 1461 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๘ สัญลักษณ์ Er เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 68, symbol Er. A metal; a soft, lustrous solid that melts at 1497 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๖๙ สัญลักษณ์ Tm เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 69, symbol Tm. A metal; a solid that melts at 1545 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗ สัญลักษณ์ N เป็นอโลหะ ลั: Element number 7, symbol N. A non-metal; a colourless, odourless gas that is chemically unreactive, making up about 80 percent of the atmosphere. It is vital to living things as a key component of proteins and nucleic acids.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๐ สัญลักษณ์ Yb เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 70, symbol Yb. A metal; a lustrous solid that melts at 824 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๑ สัญลักษณ์ Lu เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 71, symbol Lu. A metal; a soft solid that melts at 1652 °C.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๒ สัญลักษณ์ Hf เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 72, symbol Hf. A metal; a grey solid that melts at 2150 °C. Used for control rods in water-cooled nuclear reactors.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๓ สัญลักษณ์ Ta เป็นโลหะสี: Element number 73, symbol Ta. A greyish-white metal; a solid that melts at 2996 °C. Used for light bulb filaments and in alloys with other metals.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๔ สัญลักษณ์ W เป็นโลหะ ลั: Element number 74, symbol W. A metal; a grey solid that melts at 3410 °C. Used for light bulb filaments and in alloys with other metals; also called วุลแฟรม (wolfram).
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๕ สัญลักษณ์ Re เป็นโลหะลั: Element number 75, symbol Re. A metal; a grey solid that melts at 3180 °C. Used in alloys with other metals, in electrical equipment, and as a component of heat-resistant metals in rockets.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๖ สัญลักษณ์ Os เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 76, symbol Os. A metal; a very hard white solid that melts at 3000 °C. Used in alloys with other metals.

ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๘ สัญลักษณ์ Pt เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 78, symbol Pt. A metal; a lustrous silvery solid that melts at 1769 °C. Used in alloys with other metals, in electrical equipment and scientific instruments, and in high-value jewellery.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๗๙ สัญลักษณ์ Au เป็นโลหะ ล: Element number 79, symbol Au. A metal; a very soft yellow solid that melts at 1063 °C. It can be beaten into sheets less than 0.0001 millimetres thick and is used for jewellery and coinage. The purity of gold is now measured in carats, with 24-carat gold being the purest.
ธาตุลําดับที่ ๘ สัญลักษณ์ O เป็นแก๊ส มีป: Element number 8, symbol O. Essential for respiration and combustion; burned with acetylene for welding or cutting metal, and used in medicine to assist patients' breathing.

นอกจากนี้ ราชบัณฑิตยสถานได้จัดทำโครงการเ: In addition, the Royal Institute has run many projects to disseminate knowledge in various fields and to preserve and promote the Thai language, including the “Know and Love Thai” project, a key project under government policy; the ASEAN Languages and Cultures project; and the National Language Policy project. It also exchanges knowledge and coordinates with other learned societies and academic institutions in Thailand and abroad. The Royal Institute has continuously carried out its mission of study, research and the advancement of all branches of knowledge. Its best-known academic work, used as a reference and as the standard for writing Thai, both in official documents and in education, so that usage is uniform, is the Royal Institute Dictionary.

นับตั้งแต่วันที่ ๑๔ กุมภาพันธ์ พ.ศ. ๒๕๕๘: Since 14 February 2015, the agency “ราชบัณฑิตยสถาน” (Royal Institute) has been renamed “สำนักงานราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Office of the Royal Society), and “สภาราชบัณฑิต” (Council of Fellows) has been renamed “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society of Thailand), but academic work and services disseminating its work to the public continue, along with development to meet the public's needs more widely and quickly. Besides producing academic books in various fields, radio and television programmes, CDs and DVDs disseminating knowledge, and e-learning materials, in 2015 the Office of the Royal Society made its most-demanded books more usable by engaging the National Electronics and Computer Technology Center (NECTEC) to develop applications of the Royal Institute Dictionary B.E. 2554 and of How to Read and How to Write, Royal Institute edition, for use on smartphones. The Office of the Royal Society and NECTEC have also agreed to cooperate in turning other academic works into applications. In addition, the Office of the Royal Society has improved and promoted Thai-language learning for people with disabilities, for example by producing Braille editions of the Royal Institute Dictionary and How to Read and How to Write for people with visual impairments, and by holding training in correct Thai pronunciation for blind people and teachers of the blind, so that people with visual impairments and blind people can learn correct Thai pronunciation on an equal footing with others.

นายอนุชา นาคาศัย รัฐมนตรีประจำสำนักนายกร: Mr. Anucha Nakasai, Minister attached to the Prime Minister's Office, said that the Office of the Royal Society is an important agency that contributes greatly to the nation. Its academic work is not limited to language alone; many of its academic works serve as references for current research and can be used for work, study and academic citation. It preserves the Thai language sustainably, coins new terms, develops the language and passes this heritage on to future generations, transferring knowledge from the present generation to the next, including training in Thai and local dialects in each region. To ensure smooth operations, he asked the executives to plan for an adequate workforce structure and to set up information technology database systems so that both Office of the Royal Society premises can work together in a coordinated and unified manner. This is a good opportunity for the Royal Society of Thailand to transform its image into a modern digital government agency, moving into the Government 4.0 era with a focus on convenience for the public. For example, an application could let the public find the locations of both Royal Society service points, navigate to them, access a service guide and rate their satisfaction after receiving services. This responds to government policy: on 16 June 2020 the Cabinet approved, in line with the opinion of the Bureau of the Budget, funding to renovate the Chao Chom Manda Luean building into the Royal Society of Thailand History Hall, and the contract is expected to be signed before the end of September 2020.

Section 6 of the Royal Society Act B.E. 2558 states that the Royal Society of Thailand is an institution for the advancement of all branches of knowledge, founded by His Majesty King Prajadhipok, with the objective of carrying out study and research in order to disseminate, promote and exchange knowledge, and to develop, preserve and provide academic services for the benefit of the country and the people. Under Section 12, the Royal Society of Thailand has 3 types of members: 1. Associate Fellows, 2. Fellows, 3. Honorary Fellows. Section 24 of the Act establishes a council within the Office of the Royal Society, called the “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society of Thailand), consisting of the President of the Royal Society of Thailand as President of the Council, 2 Vice Presidents of the Royal Society of Thailand as Vice Presidents of the Council, and all Fellows as council members, with the Secretary-General of the Office of the Royal Society serving as Secretary of the Council and the Deputy Secretary-General serving as Assistant Secretary of the Council.

รัฐมนตรีประจำสำนักนายกรัฐมนตรี กล่าวเพิ่: The Minister attached to the Prime Minister's Office added that the Office of the Royal Society has always served as the principal organization for preserving and promoting the use of the Thai language. Its activities, such as Thai language skills competitions for young people and awards for outstanding users of Thai, are good projects that build competitiveness and strengthen human potential. Today is a highly competitive digital age; if the Office of the Royal Society adds online sales channels for its academic works or produces e-books, it will reduce paper use, offer greater convenience and speed, meet public needs and adapt to Government 4.0, or a digital-era government focused on public convenience. It should develop into a modern service organization, honor the Fellows of the Royal Society as revered persons of the nation to inspire young people with good role models, become a source of accurate knowledge and understanding about the monarchy and royal duties, and add more channels for academic services so the public can access them more easily.

ราชา ศัพท์ที่นำมาแสดงนี้เป็นส่วนหนึ่งของ: The royal vocabulary shown here is part of the royal vocabulary for which the Royal Institute's Committee on Guidelines for the Use of the Thai Language is considering usage guidelines. The words selected here are those whose royal-vocabulary form is the same for every rank, namely for use with the King, Somdet Phra Borommarachininat (Her Majesty the Queen), Somdet Phra Borommarachini (the Queen), His Royal Highness the Crown Prince, Her Royal Highness Princess Maha Chakri Sirindhorn, and members of the royal family of the ranks of Somdet Chao Fa, Phra Ong Chao and Mom Chao. Royal vocabulary also differs according to the rank of the royal person. Moreover, even when it is known which royal word is used for an ordinary word, and with the King or royal persons of which rank, one must still consider the context or surrounding text of the sentence or passage in which the royal word is used, so that the meaning is conveyed correctly and clearly.

Today (21 August 2020) at 09:00, Mr. Anucha Nakhasai, Minister Attached to the Prime Minister's Office, visited the Office of the Royal Society to attend a meeting of the Office of the Royal Society's Civil Service Sub-Committee acting as the Ministerial Civil Service Sub-Committee, welcomed by Dr. Duangta Tancho, Secretary-General of the Office of the Royal Society, together with executives, civil servants and staff. At 10:00 he went to survey the Residence of Chao Chom Manda Luean, a historic building for which the Office of the Royal Society has received budget approval for renovation into an office and history hall of the Royal Society of Thailand, separate from the offices of the Office of the Royal Society, which are expected to move from Sanam Suea Pa to the Government Complex Commemorating His Majesty the King's 80th Birthday Anniversary, 5th December B.E. 2550, Zone C, around early 2024. He then returned to visit and give policy guidance to the Office of the Royal Society in the 4th-floor meeting room from 11:00 to 12:00

In the center of the Royal Sword is an open book inscribed with the word “bandito”, signifying that Fellows of the Royal Society are armed with knowledge.

The emblem depicts the Great Crown of Victory, symbolizing the King, above an upright sacred sword. At the center of the sword is an open book bearing the word “ปณฺฑิโต” (pandito), signifying Fellows of the Royal Society whose wisdom is likened to a weapon. Behind the sword and the book are rays radiating all around, signifying the light of wisdom. Below is a ribbon whose two ends curve up to meet the side flaps of the Great Crown. The green of the ribbon is the color of the birthday of His Majesty King Prajadhipok, who graciously established the Royal Society of Thailand on 19 April 1926. Beneath the Great Crown emblem, the words “Office of the Royal Society” curve along the ribbon

On 19 April 1926, His Majesty King Prajadhipok, King Rama VII of the Chakri Dynasty, graciously proclaimed the establishment of the “ราชบัณฑิตยสภา” (Royal Society). The King saw fit to revive the work of the Krom Ratchabandit, an ancient department and a position to which those learned in the arts and sciences were appointed to serve the Crown. Later, in 1933, the House of Representatives advised His Majesty King Prajadhipok that a Royal Institute should be established, with members of learning who might in future be elected as Fellows, to carry out research and disseminate knowledge to the public and to produce textbooks widely. His Majesty therefore graciously enacted the Royal Institute Act in 1933 and repealed the proclamation establishing the Royal Society dated 19 April 1926.

เมื่อวันพฤหัสบดีที่ 21 December 2017 ณ ห: On Thursday, 21 December 2017, at Grand Ballroom 1, Maneechan Resort, Chanthaburi Province, at the 13th seminar on the National Memory of the World Register, Mr. Kritsada Bunyasamit, Associate Fellow, Academy of Moral and Political Sciences, and Chair of the Committee for the Revision and Study of Ancient Thai Law, Office of the Royal Society, proposed registering the Three Seals Law as national documentary heritage and Memory of the World documentary heritage in honor of His Majesty King Buddha Yodfa Chulaloke the Great, with Professor Sawaeng Bunchaloemwiphat as commentator. The Three Seals Law is a compilation of Thai laws from the Ayutthaya period, which King Rama I ordered to be categorized and revised; it has been in use for over 500 years and shows the historical evolution of Thailand in politics, government, economy, society, arts and culture. As the only existing set, it is irreplaceable and therefore important at both national and global levels

Thai words pronounced "ban" can be written in several ways, such as บรร, บัน and บรรณ, because each word has a different origin and is formed differently. 2. Words with บรร may come from Khmer, e.g. บรรทม (banthom) from ผทํ; from Sanskrit and Pali, e.g. บรรถร (banthon) from Pali ปตฺถร and Sanskrit ปฺรสฺตร; or may be derived from Thai words, e.g. บรรสาน (bansan) derived from ประสาน (prasan). Learners should consult dictionaries and academic texts on the Thai language and remember the origin or derivation of each word
๑. ชื่อ “ปุณชรัศมิ์” แยกศัพท์ได้เป็นคำว่: 1. The name “ปุณชรัศมิ์” (Punnacharat) can be broken down as: - “ปุณ” from Pali “ปุณฺณ”, meaning full - “ช” from Pali and Sanskrit, meaning born - “รัศมิ์” from Sanskrit “รศฺมิ”, meaning light. Therefore, “ปุณชรัศมิ์” can be translated as “light born in fullness”. 2. The name “ปุญชรัสมิ์” (Punyacharat) can be broken down as: - “ปุญ” from Pali “ปุญฺ?”, meaning merit - “ช” from Pali and Sanskrit, meaning born - “รัสมิ์” resembles a word of Pali and Sanskrit origin, but it was not found in Pali or Sanskrit dictionaries. Since not every part of the name “ปุญชรัสมิ์” can be given a meaning, the name as a whole cannot be interpreted
